It is caused by the fungus Venturia inaequalis and can lead to the formation of red, brown, or black spots on the leaves, fruits, and branches.

To treat apple scab, it is essential to practice proper tree care and maintenance. This includes:

1. Pruning: Regularly pruning the tree can help to remove infected branches and prevent the spread of the disease.
2. Fertilization: Ensuring the tree receives adequate nutrients can help to strengthen its immune system and make it more resistant to diseases.
3. Pest control: Controlling pests, such as aphids and other insects, can help to prevent the spread of the disease.
4. Fungicide application: Applying a fungicide to the tree during the early stages of the disease can help to prevent its spread and reduce the severity of the symptoms.

By following these steps, you can help to manage apple scab and maintain the health of your fruit tree.

By following these practices, you can help prevent the spread of bacterial soft rot and maintain a healthy growing environment for your plants.
